title: BHSM Museum recorded visitor tour
pronunciation: BHSM expanded to spoken letters B H S M; all other words follow the visitor tour.

tracks.title: Begin with a field excitation.
tracks.transcript: Begin with a field excitation. Start with the lifecycle scene. BHSM interprets particle structure through geometric organization. The field lines make an excitation visible, and the changing pattern introduces the idea of a localized mode. Follow this illustrative unstable excitation through propagation to a decay event, where daughter excitations appear. The animation supplies a visual sequence; its durations, paths and outgoing modes are schematic. Use the pause button or select a phase to examine what changes. A physical decay calculation would also need the permitted interaction channels, conservation laws and a quantitative rate. Look for the moment when the parent becomes outgoing states.

tracks.title: Read the map from the core upward.
tracks.transcript: Read the map from the core upward. Read the scale map from bottom to top: hypersphere core; excitations and moiré-like modes; Standard Model particles; atoms and the periodic table; molecules; planets and stars; and cosmic structure. The Standard Model occupies one slice in this broader BHSM picture. The core is a proposed foundation without an assigned ordinary diameter or internal travel time. The slices organize ideas across scales, while the moiré pattern illustrates the proposed organization of modes. Select each slice to see its meaning and evidence status. Each connection still needs its own physical explanation and tests. Notice where the labels change from BHSM proposal to established science.

tracks.title: Distinguish the framework from the proposal.
tracks.transcript: Distinguish the framework from the proposal. Open the Standard Model chart and look at the quarks, leptons, interaction bosons and Higgs. This is the established particle framework used as a reference in the museum. BHSM proposes a geometric interpretation and conditionally reproduces the matter and gauge ledger under stated assumptions. That conditional structural result has a specific scope. Particle masses, interaction probabilities and cosmological responses each require further physical constructions and independent checks. The conventional minimal Standard Model also leaves neutrino masses outside its original field content. Use the exhibit labels to keep established references, conditional results and proposed interpretations distinct. Ask which parts are measured references and which are BHSM claims.

tracks.title: Turn a picture into a testable question.
tracks.transcript: Turn a picture into a testable question. Finish at the evidence guide. Choose one claim and follow its source. Look for what was assumed, what was calculated, the result’s stated scope and the observations used for comparison. A physical prediction must be fixed independently of the measured answer it will face. Historical numerical screens and certified calculations on specified backgrounds retain those classifications. Useful questions include: which observable follows from the construction, what could falsify it, and can another researcher reproduce the result? Follow the current research record for the unresolved steps. The museum invites careful exploration, independent checking and specific criticism. Choose one claim you would like to reproduce or test.
